summary.text: The paper adds a learned gate that scores each retrieved passage against the question before a fusion-in-decoder reader attends to it,
and reports +2.1 EM on NQ and +3.4 on HotpotQA over FiD-base with a smaller adapter.

strengths.text: A simple, cheap change that composes with any retriever and reader.
Baselines are re-run with the authors' code rather than copied.

spans.text: All numbers are on development sets, which were also used for model selection; test-set results are needed to support the claims.
The TriviaQA gain of 0.3 EM is within the ±0.4 standard deviation, yet the abstract lists it as an improvement.
The compute budget is not reported, so the efficiency claim cannot be checked.

questions.text: How often is the gold passage missing from the retrieved set, and what does the gate do then?
Does one gate trained on NQ transfer to HotpotQA?

missing_experiments.text: Test-set results on NQ and HotpotQA.
An ablation of the gate's inputs (question only, passage only).

spans.text: A useful, well-executed idea whose headline gains are clear on two benchmarks; the development-set-only evaluation keeps it from a clear accept.
